newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels kill five soldiers in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels kill five soldiers in ambush.

text.p: Leftist rebels killed five soldiers and wounded 17 on Sunday in the first major attack in Colombia's southern Caqueta province since part of the region was temporarily demilitarized earlier this month, an army chief said.

The attack took place in a rural zone of the municipality of Solano as a combined army and marine force was checking boats passing up and down the River Orteguaza, one of the main thoroughfares through the isolated jungle region.

Gen. Agustin Ardila, head of the army's Fourth Division, blamed the killings on the so-called Southern Bloc of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), Latin America's oldest and largest guerrilla army.

"The ambush took place as we were carrying out registration and control operations along the River Orteguaza. Two of the dead were marines and the three others were infantrymen," Ardila told reporters.
Some of the injured were flown to hospitals in Bogota for treatment, army sources said.

The attack was just outside a 5,000 square mile (13,000 sq km) zone recently demilitarized to allow the FARC to release 70 troops, some of whom were taken prisoner more than nine months earlier. Troops were only permitted to return to the demilitarized area last Tuesday.

The FARC's Southern Bloc is headed by Cmdr. Joaquin Gomez. In an recent interview with Reuters, Gomez said the FARC would not flee the area once the army returned and warned his forces were ready if necessary to step up attacks on the military.

Gomez has become one of the biggest thorns in the side of the Colombian military after he ordered an attack in southern Narino province in early 1996 in which 31 soldiers died and last August's devastating raid on the Las Delicias base in neighbouring Putumayo province in which 31 more soldiers were killed and 60 were taken prisoner.
